headline: Maui County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee
meeting.summary: The committee questioned staff on buying two water systems sold as one package; Council Member Sugimura's committee takes it up August 4th.
meeting.recap: Staff said the County's purchase agreement covers only the water systems' assets, not the companies themselves.[[0:14:47]] Staff said using this water for existing County needs would still require a water use permit.[[0:47:14]] Staff believe the County would get easements (rights to use land), not the land under the assets.[[0:48:38]] Staff said only the PUC must approve the purchase itself.[[0:50:42]] Staff said a nearby fire station's water use should already be covered by existing permits, but they will double-check.[[0:52:58]] A council member said sustainable yield is not a target to pump up to and leaves out cultural uses.[[0:59:18]] The department said Council Member Sugimura's committee will take up the purchase August 4th.[[1:07:27]] If approved there, it goes to the council for final approval.[[1:07:54]] If the council acts in August, closing could come around April of next year.[[1:08:11]] The chair asked to defer, or postpone, the item if no one objected.[[1:09:04]]
meeting.next: Committee staff will send follow-up questions, with answers hoped for by the August 4th meeting. After council approval, the department will move forward with the PUC process.

moments.q: "Doesn't mean that we use up all seven million gallons per day."
Managing director corrects who owns the water companies
"This is a really good deal for the community."
